summary: Plan-first workflows can delay learning, anchor teams to an incorrect design, and overwhelm reviewers with plausible prose.

points.text: Exploratory tasks reveal their constraints through small edits, builds, and experiments. A read-only phase may produce a detailed plan based on assumptions that one reversible prototype would quickly disprove.
Fluent plans create an illusion of coverage. Reviewers may approve named files and steps without noticing a missing security boundary, migration consequence, or unstated product decision.
Mandatory approval for routine, reversible work adds latency and notification fatigue, encouraging blanket approvals that weaken control for genuinely risky plans.
A plan becomes stale as the branch, dependencies, or requirements change. Reusing it without binding input revisions and freshness checks can be worse than replanning.
